item.title: Vegapay Bags $10 Mn To Scale Credit Line On UPI Infrastructure
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Mumbai-based fintech startup Vegapay has raised $10 Mn (₹92.3 Cr) in a Series A funding round co-led by Vertex Ventures…
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai-based fintech startup Vegapay has raised $10 Mn (₹92.3 Cr) in a Series A funding round co-led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia and India and Prosus.

The round also saw participation from existing investors Elevation Capital and Eximius Ventures.

The funding round comprises both primary and secondary transactions, with over 40 employees getting an opportunity to sell a portion of their vested employee stock ownership plans (ESOPs).

It will deploy the fresh capital to onboard more banks onto its credit line on UPI platform, introduce secured credit lines backed by fixed deposits, gold and mutual funds, and expand its credit card, prepaid card and forex card programmes. It also plans to strengthen its engineering and risk teams.

Founded in 2022 by Gaurav Mittal, Himanshu Agrawal and Puneet Sharma, Vegapay provides a technology platform that enables banks to launch and manage Credit Line on UPI (CLOU), credit card and other credit programmes.

Its platform allows banks to run multiple co-branded credit programmes, each with independent limits, pricing and rules. Banks can also deploy the technology on their own cloud infrastructure or on-premises.

The startup claims to command a majority of India’s Credit Line on UPI market as of November 2026. Its platform is live with YES BANK, Unity Small Finance Bank, Suryoday Small Finance Bank and BOBCARD.

It also powers credit programmes for fintech and consumer-facing platforms, including Paytm, BharatPe, Kiwi UPI, Scapia and EbixCash World Money.

Betting On Credit Line On UPI

Vegapay’s fundraise comes as Credit Line on UPI emerges as a new distribution channel for formal credit in India.

The offering allows banks to provide customers with pre-sanctioned credit lines that can be used to make payments at UPI QR codes through existing payment applications, without requiring a separate credit card or app.

While UPI has transformed India’s digital payments ecosystem, the integration of credit into the payment network could create another avenue for banks to distribute lending products.

Vegapay is positioning its platform as the underlying technology layer for banks looking to launch these products without building the entire infrastructure in-house.

“UPI was India’s payments revolution. Credit Line on UPI is the UPI moment for credit, and banks should lead it,” said Gaurav Mittal, cofounder and CEO of Vegapay.

item.title: IT Secy Defends Sarvam’s Token Factory Over Chinese LLM Debate
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Reacting to the ongoing controversy around Sarvam AI hosting Chinese AI models on its new inference service Token Factory, MeitY…
item.content:encoded:
Reacting to the ongoing controversy around Sarvam AI hosting Chinese AI models on its new inference service Token Factory, MeitY secretary S Krishnan has reportedly said that offering overseas LLMs does not constitute a violation of the principles of the IndiaAI Mission.

“I don’t think there is any contradiction between what they (Sarvam) are doing for the IndiaAI mission and working towards the frontier model which will come in years and what they are offering now is a service in the AI space,” said Krishnan as per Business Standard.

Defending Sarvam’s Token Factory, the MeitY secretary said that it was the company’s imperative to monetise its offering, adding that Sarvam’s work on development of the indigenous AI model is different from its inference platform. 

“After all, AI companies also require a revenue model. They need a model in which they can monetise revenues and many other such experiments have been tried,” he reportedly said.

As per news agency PTI, Krishnan also said that the government now also plans to work on a scheme to support AI inference. 

This comes a week after Sarvam debuted the Token Factory. The new offering lets enterprises access Indian and global AI models through a single API while running workloads on GPUs in India. Besides Sarvam’s own 105B model, the platform also offers access to overseas open-weight models from Google, DeepSeek, GLM and Kimi. 

Quickly after the launch, critics raised questions over Token Factory hosting Chinese models despite Sarvam positioning itself as a champion of sovereign Indian AI. Many also raised questions over whether reliance on foreign open-weight models dilutes Sarvam’s push for homegrown AI capability.

Pushing back against criticism, the AI unicorn said that the offering relies strictly on privately procured GPUs and not state-sponsored subsidies. It also said that Token Factory will create a new commercial opportunity for the company, reduce latency and trim India’s dependence on overseas token platforms.

To prove that inference hosting has not diluted its core research mission, Sarvam subsequently also rolled out its upgraded Sarvam-105B-1711 model and a dictation API for English and 22 other Indian languages.

Addressing reporters on Wednesday, Krishnan also said that the ministry has also gathered feedback from startups and entities regarding Sarvam’s services. 

“I think based on what Sarvam has told us, based on the experience that people have, we do not see any misuse of the support which the India AI mission has provided to Sarvam in the service that they are now offering,” Krishnan reportedly added.

Going forward, Krishnan added that the government also plans to support the startup’s work towards a trillion-parameter model.

item.title: Delhi Police Arrests Four Suspects In Crypto Fraud Case
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: A Delhi Police cyber team has busted an alleged organised cryptocurrency fraud syndicate.  In a statement, additional deputy commissioner of…
item.content:encoded:
A Delhi Police cyber team has busted an alleged organised cryptocurrency fraud syndicate. 

In a statement, additional deputy commissioner of Police for Delhi’s South-West district, Kumar Abhishek, said that the cyber team has arrested four members of the syndicate, including alleged mastermind Atul Meena.

The arrests come after a trader approached the Police in connection with a phishing scam that drained 4,985 USDT, valued at around ₹5 Lakh, from his wallet back in June.

The victim had allegedly attempted to sell USDT via a P2P transaction on crypto exchange Binance on June 6 when a purported buyer convinced him to move the discussion to WhatsApp. The victim claims to have then unsuspectingly clicked a phishing link that granted unauthorised wallet access to the syndicate, resulting in the entire balance being transferred. 

Afterwards, the victim filed a complaint with the Police and a case was registered in the matter on July 2. 

Using call records, IP logs and WhatsApp data, the officials traced the suspects’ operations to Rajasthan’s Alwar, where they were recruiting local youth to join the alleged syndicate on a profit-sharing basis. 

The recruits allegedly procured SIM cards and set up WhatsApp accounts to source USDT sellers. Once sellers responded, their numbers were passed to Meena to execute the phishing pitch. 

Abhishek said that the cyber team raided Meena’s hideout in Alwar and also arrested three of his associates from Jaipur – Jagmohan Meena, Narender Kumar Meena and Manish Meena – before ultimately apprehending Atul near Dhaula Kuan in Delhi.

Besides the four arrests, they also recovered ₹1.6 Lakh in cash, 11 mobile phones, one iPad, one Wi-Fi router and six SIM cards during the course of the probe. 

Police said the complainant has been refunded the entire sum and they are examining the transaction logs and exchange wallets to identify the accounts linked to the syndicate. 

This comes as law enforcement agencies scrutinise the Indian crypto ecosystem over links with organised criminal rings. Earlier this month, the ED provisionally attached around ₹14.2 Cr worth of assets linked to crypto platform HashPe, alleging it was operating a fraudulent crypto-based Ponzi investment scheme. 

Five Bengaluru-based platforms also came under the directorate’s scanner in June when ED searched their premises and froze their accounts having ₹6 Cr worth assets in total. The ED then had said that these platforms used VDAs to enable unauthorised cross-border transactions. 

This comes as the regulatory treatment of cryptos remains an ongoing debate in India. While the government does not recognise cryptocurrencies as legal tender, crypto platforms have to strictly comply with money laundering regulation. At the same time, income from VDAs attracts 30% capital gains tax and 1% TDS. 

Policymakers have been cautious to introduce a legal framework around crypto given concerns over money laundering, terror financing, cyber fraud and offshore capital flows. Earlier this year, at a meeting of the parliamentary standing committee on finance to discuss the same, senior government officials told the panel that they consider the sector “high-risk”.

item.title: Kalyan Krishnamurthy’s Exit: How Walmart’s Kickback Probe, IPO Delay Shook Up Flipkart
item.dc:creator: Bismah Malik
item.description: Walmart has asked Flipkart Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down, three sources aware of the development told Inc42 as…
item.content:encoded:
Walmart has asked Flipkart Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down, three sources aware of the development told Inc42 as the investigations into alleged seller kickbacks widen across the company.

The probe, which was initially reported to cover Flipkart’s smartphones and luggage and travel accessories (LTA) categories, has now expanded across the group, including fashion ecommerce platform Myntra and travel booking platform Cleartrip, the sources added.

According to the three sources, the investigation has unearthed kickbacks across the various companies within the group with some of the top executives allegedly involved in receiving kickbacks from preferential sellers, brands for enhanced visibility and sourcing of materials. 

One of the sources said that Walmart had earlier asked CFO, Sriram Venkataraman to step down following reports of financial irregularities/ kickbacks at the firm.

Notably, Venkataraman announced his exit in March 2026

Additionally, sources said the decision to ask Krishnamurthy to step down is also tied to a delayed IPO timeline for Flipkart and to achieving the ecommerce company’s profitability target.

“Walmart has been firm that Flipkart must speed up its IPO process and improve profitability, and has appointed consulting firm McKinsey to carry out a pre-assessment of the company’s IPO readiness”, the sources said.

Walmart also questioned Flipkart’s expansion into new verticals such as food delivery and microdramas, among other ventures, which it saw as delaying the IPO, they added. 

All of these factors together led to Walmart asking Krishnamurthy to step down, the sources said.

Sources also indicated that the ecommerce major may also see more senior-level exits following the departure of Krishnamurthy from the firm.

The ecommerce giant issued a statement confirming Krishnamurthy’s exit, but it did not reveal the reason for the leadership change. Sources added that the parent company decided to make a change after Krishnamurthy’s decade-long stint at the helm.

In an official statement on Wednesday, the company did not indicate that this was about the Walmart investigation. Instead, Flipkart said the overall business grew more than fivefold during his tenure. 

Incidentally, Krishnamurthy’s statement on his exit touched on ethics and integrity, in addition to business growth. “I am proud of the scale of the business we have built, but equally proud of how we have built it. Strong ethics, integrity and high standards of governance have been central to Flipkart’s growth,” Krishnamurthy said in the statement.

Flipkart said it will appoint a successor in the coming weeks. 

Balaji Thiagarajan, currently Flipkart’s chief product and technology officer, will lead the company in the interim, along with the Flipkart board.

“Both Flipkart and Walmart are better because of Kalyan. We are grateful for his leadership, the governance he instilled and his many contributions to the company,” Chris Nicholas, president and CEO of Walmart International, said in a statement.

Inc42 has reached out to Flipkart with queries on the probe and the circumstances of Krishnamurthy’s exit. The story will be updated as and when the ecommerce company responds.

What Led To The Ouster 

Sources told Inc42 that the investigation unearthed kickbacks across Flipkart’s sourcing, manufacturing, logistics, and design teams, as well as its group companies.

Executives allegedly took commissions from sellers to boost their visibility on the platform and compromised the quality of material sourced for Flipkart’s private-label business, the sources said.

“This has been going on for several years and is largely a compliance issue,” one source said. 

The wider scope of the probe today compared to 2024 is largely because of a precedent of such allegations at the Flipkart group. 

Sources said a key member of Myntra’s design team quit over similar allegations a few years ago, followed by a similar resignation at Flipkart.

The most recent probe was sparked after sellers directly approached Walmart with complaints about being asked to pay a kickback fee for greater visibility on Flipkart. This prompted the parent company to act. 

Things came to a head in late October 2026, when Walmart launched an investigation following the whistleblower complaints. 

Reports speculated that Flipkart employees received kickbacks of over INR 150 Cr (about $16 Mn) from vendors; however, the actual amount has not been officially revealed. 

The allegations pertain to employees offering vendors preferential treatment, including greater visibility on the platform, in return for payments and favours. In the smartphones category, employees allegedly took cuts from vendors as devices moved between businesses, including through Flipkart’s B2B operations.

However, the extent of the alleged kickbacks and the number of employees involved is not yet clear.

This was reportedly Walmart’s third such investigation at Flipkart in less than three years. 

US retail behemoth’s second concern has been a mega listing of Flipkart, which has now missed its deadline for a few years in a row.

“Walmart was also concerned about the recent performance of Flipkart during its flagship Big Billions Day Sales and is particularly not happy with the core marketplace business performance,” a company insider told Inc42.

In Walmart’s Q3 FY27 earnings call last week, CFO John David Rainey said the sale’s timing created a 100 basis point headwind to Walmart’s top line growth in Q3, and that the Big Billion Days performance “will be reported in International’s fourth quarter results this year”. 

The ecommerce major had been preparing for a listing for years, and after completing its reverse flip from Singapore to India in March 2026, it was expected to go public in late 2026 or early 2027. 

It was also exploring a pre-IPO round of about $2.5 Bn. Those plans were put on hold in May, when Walmart reportedly asked Flipkart to pause fundraising and focus on profitability, pushing the IPO to at least 2028.

Kalyan Krishnamurthy’s Exit Leaves A Vacuum 

Krishnamurthy’s exit is the first major leadership change in Flipkart since the acquisition by Walmart in 2018. 

He joined the company in 2016 from Tiger Global, one of the early investors in Flipkart. Soon after that, he was appointed as Flipkart CEO in January 2017, and then took over as group CEO in 2018 after cofounder Binny Bansal resigned following an investigation into allegations of personal misconduct. 

As CEO, Krishnamurthy became the face of the company into its second decade, after founders Sachin Bansal and Binny Bansal had led the company from 2007 to 2017. 

And now, as Flipkart enters its third decade, and prepares for a potential IPO in the near future, it will be led by a new CEO and there could be other changes in the offing, given recent headlines around an IPO

The CEO’s exit comes at a time when Flipkart is already dealing with a string of senior departures and discontent among former employees over delayed ESOP buybacks, even as other companies have listed and executed buybacks.  

As reported, more than 1,000 former Flipkart Group employees had earlier approached Walmart’s board seeking equal access to stock buybacks offered to current staff. The leadership churn now adds to the uncertainty around Flipkart’s IPO plans. 

Krishnamurthy had said in July that the company had no timeline for going public, while Walmart has reportedly asked Flipkart to hit EBITDA breakeven by the end of March 2027 before pursuing an IPO or a fresh funding round.

In FY26, Flipkart’s consolidated operating revenue rose 18% YoY to INR 1,45,880 Cr, while its net loss narrowed marginally to INR 8,468 Cr from INR 8,646 Cr in FY25. The consolidated numbers include Myntra and Cleartrip, following Flipkart’s redomiciling to India.

While the first phase of Flipkart’s journey was defined by its founders, the previous ten years have seen the company branch out into new categories, such as the Cleartrip acquisition, the fintech push, the foray into food delivery, and of course the aggressive investments for its quick commerce app Flipkart Minutes. 

All this means the incoming CEO will have to lead a Flipkart that’s vastly different from the company that Krishnamurthy inherited. Whoever steps in will have big shoes to fill. 

[Edited By Nikhil Subramaniam]

item.title: Navi Crosses 5% UPI Market Share As PhonePe, Google Pay Slip In October
item.dc:creator: Md Zakariya Khan
item.description: Sachin Bansal-led Navi continued to strengthen its position in the UPI ecosystem in October 2026. The fintech platform’s share in…
item.content:encoded:
Sachin Bansal-led Navi continued to strengthen its position in the UPI ecosystem in October 2026. The fintech platform’s share in the UPI market crossed the 5% mark over the past month, data released by NPCI revealed.  

Of the 25.47 Bn processed by UPI, transactions processed by Navi platform rose to 5.04% from 4.76% in September. Overall, Navi hosted 1.27 Bn UPI transactions during the month, an 11% increase from 1.14 Bn in September

The fintech platform processed around 1.27 Bn UPI transactions during the month, up from 1.14 Bn in September. 

Navi’s gains came as the UPI leaders — PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm — continued to see some decline in their market share in October. Taken together, the three platforms still combine over 85% of India’s UPI market.

PhonePe remained the largest UPI app, with a 45.34% share of transaction volume, down from 45.57% in September. Google Pay’s share fell to 32.09% from 32.23%, while Paytm’s share declined to 7.96% from 8.12%.

Navi Overtakes CRED In UPI Transaction Value

Navi’s growth was also visible in transaction value. The platform processed UPI transactions worth ₹62,492 Cr in October, marginally ahead of CRED’s ₹62,102 Cr, according to NPCI data. This made Navi the fourth-largest UPI app by transaction value, ending CRED’s position in the ranking after more than five years.

Among other emerging platforms, WhatsApp’s share increased to 0.85% in October from 0.80% in September. FamApp by Trio also recorded a rise to 0.99% from 0.95%, while BHIM’s share edged up to 1.07% from 1.06%.

On the other hand, super.money’s share declined to 1.65% from 1.69%. CRED maintained its share at 0.59%, while Amazon Pay’s share increased marginally to 0.40% from 0.38%.

The data indicates that while PhonePe and Google Pay continue to control a large part of India’s UPI market, smaller players such as Navi are gradually expanding their presence. Navi’s latest gains also come amid growing competition among fintech platforms to capture a larger share of India’s digital payments market.

item.title: Beyond Its Sovereignty Bet, What’s Sarvam Really Mining?
item.dc:creator: Ankush Das
item.description: Last week, Sarvam AI found itself in the eye of a storm. The poster child of India’s sovereign AI ambitions…
item.content:encoded:
Last week, Sarvam AI found itself in the eye of a storm. The poster child of India’s sovereign AI ambitions drew flak for offering access to Chinese AI models, including DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM, through its newly launched inference platform, Token Factory.

The point of contention among critics has been whether a startup that received government support to build indigenous AI models should be in the business of selling access to Chinese models. Sarvam clarified that its Token Factory runs on privately procured GPUs, and its inference business does not dilute the ambition to build homegrown AI models.

Amid this controversy, the AI unicorn has expanded its product portfolio with two new launches — Sarvam-105B-1711, an upgraded version of its existing large language model (LLM), and Sarvam Dictate, a speech-to-text API that supports English and 22 Indian languages.

The launches offer a glimpse into Sarvam’s larger game plan. The unicorn wants to offer Indian enterprises everything they need to build and deploy AI. From homegrown AI models and the infrastructure to run them to voice AI, coding agents and workplace applications, Sarvam desires to become a one-stop shop for enterprise AI in India.

Not to mention, Sarvam’s full-stack AI ambition has begun to find commercial traction, particularly in the financial services sector, including Tata Capital and Mahindra Finance. The latter has also deployed Sarvam-powered voice agents across sales, collections and frontline employee engagement. It claims to have executed 1 Cr+ customer calls via its voice stack.

At Bolna’s Symphony 2026 last week, Vivek Raghavan, the cofounder of Sarvam AI, claimed that the company was clocking more than 3 Mn minutes a day and had crossed a billion API calls a month for its voice AI business.

At its flagship AI event, Epoch, in July this year, Sarvam unveiled a stack spanning foundation models, inference, coding, voice, document intelligence and workplace agents. Its voice agents had already handled 325 Mn minutes of conversations, while its Indus platform brought together voice, work, document, content and coding agents.

So, how do the pieces of Sarvam’s existing strategy fit together?

Sarvam Punches Above Its Weight

Sarvam-105B-1711 is not a completely new model. It is a post-trained checkpoint of the existing 105B, with Sarvam using its upgraded Blackwell infrastructure and reinforcement-learning stack to improve performance on specific workloads.

According to Ankit Jha, a machine learning engineer at Warner Bros. Discovery, post-training allows a company to improve its existing model for particular use cases or edge cases. It is also a common industry practice, with major labs routinely improving existing checkpoints rather than training an entirely new model from scratch.

In Sarvam’s case, the original 105B was trained on H100 GPUs, while the post-training runs were carried out on newer Blackwell infrastructure. Jha said Sarvam’s investment in its own technology for training, running and compressing AI models has helped it improve its reinforcement learning capabilities.

The results are worth looking at. According to Sarvam, its average score across eight conversational-agent benchmarks has grown from 42.6 to 73.9. Its Indic suite score reached 79.1, while the model also posted 89.7 on AIME 26 and 80.4 on GPQA Diamond. On the conversational-agent benchmark average, Sarvam puts the model at 73.9 against 74.0 for Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite.

The significance is not that Sarvam has suddenly overtaken the major global labs. Some of its numbers remain behind larger frontier models on reasoning, coding and knowledge benchmarks. What has changed is the distance between Sarvam and the efficient tier of open models, particularly for workloads where deployment cost, Indian languages and data control matter.

Jha said that the model could be a strong option for organisations that want to run AI with less than 100 GB of VRAM. Its roughly 65 GB quantised version can fit into the memory of a high-end workstation-class GPU, opening up a local-AI route that is difficult with much larger models. This is crucial for Indian banks and corporates that may not want sensitive workloads to leave their environments. 

The engineering underneath the model is just as important. According to Sarvam, its B200 training setup doubled pretraining throughput from 5,500 to 10,900 tokens per second per GPU, while reinforcement-learning steps fell from about 13 minutes to seven. Its 4-bit version can generate around 6,000 tokens per second per B200 across 64 concurrent users.

The Expanding Application Layer 

Sarvam is not just building the brains behind AI but also the tools that put them to work. Dictate is a clear example. The API turns speech into the text a speaker intended to write, rather than simply transcribing every word literally. 

It supports English and 22 Indian languages and requires 40% fewer character edits than Gemini 3.5 Transcribe in English and 47% fewer in Indian languages and Hinglish.

Kivi, Sarvam’s voice-based desktop application, lets users dictate across applications on Mac and is positioned as an alternative to products such as Wispr Flow. Kivi also understands more than 22 Indian languages, including code-switching, while its Epoch roadmap lists Android among the next platforms.

Kivi and Dictate sit at different points in the same stack. Kivi is the end-user application, while Dictate turns the underlying speech and language capabilities into an API that developers can embed into their products.

Sarvam also offers a document-intelligence API, Extract. It pulls structured information from documents so developers can route it into their own products. 

With Extract, Dictate and Kivi, the company has extended its playbook to include voice and documents.

Finding The Next Thing 

Sarvam has also raised substantial capital to pursue its full-stack ambition. Its $234 Mn Series B, led by HCLTech at a $1.5 Bn valuation, gives it the financial firepower to build models, infrastructure and enterprise products at the same time.

It is also building for enterprises that care about where their AI runs. Its Token Factory provides access to Sarvam’s models, along with other open-weight models, while the company offers India-based inference and dedicated GPU capacity for its BFSI customers.

A bank could use Sarvam’s models, run inference within India, deploy voice agents for customer interactions, use document and workplace agents internally, and build specialised applications around the same infrastructure. The value proposition is not necessarily that Sarvam has the best model for every task, but that it is increasingly able to provide several of those layers under one roof.

There is, however, a debate around its India-first positioning. The cofounder and CEO of Smallest.ai, Sudarshan Kamath, argues that Indian-language intelligence alone may not be enough to compete in broader knowledge work, where global models benefit from enormous amounts of English-language data. 

One practical way to judge that is to look at actual developer usage and whether developers choose Sarvam over alternatives such as Qwen or Gemini.

“Sarvam can have an advantage in Indian languages and still struggle to become the default model for coding, research or general enterprise knowledge work,” Kamath said.

But Sarvam does not need to win every category. The company no longer has to prove that it can train a large Indian-language model. It is increasingly showing that it can build the layers around that model, from inference and deployment to voice, agents and consumer applications.

The latest 105B checkpoint and Dictate matter because they extend that strategy rather than replace it. Sarvam spent much of 2026 putting the pieces together. The next phase will show whether those pieces can become a durable enterprise AI stack.

[Edited by Shishir Parasher]
[Creatives by Varshita Srivastava]

item.title: Bound By Local Laws: Meta Tells Congress Amid Content Moderation Row
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Amid protests, Meta has reportedly told Congress leaders that it was bound by local laws to take down flagged content…
item.content:encoded:
Amid protests, Meta has reportedly told Congress leaders that it was bound by local laws to take down flagged content and accounts from its platforms. Denying accusations of political favouritism, the tech giant reiterated that it was neutral towards all parties in India.

In a closed-door meeting with Congress leadership today, Meta India executives Aman Jain and Natasha Jog reportedly cited that the removals were in fact linked to its policies on AI-generated content. To this, Congress, whose youth wing (Indian Youth Congress) has been protesting against steep numbers of takedowns on Meta platforms, cited use of AI-generated BJP posts that remained accessible. 

 IYC has called for Meta restore accounts restricted following government directions and explain how its algorithms identify and take down posts. The tech giant, on the other hand, has raised concerns about protests targeting its offices and posters depicting CEO Mark Zuckerberg in RSS traditional attire. 

Meanwhile, IYC workers continued their protest, protesting outside the Bengaluru office today. “Stop dodging accountability, disclose government takedown requests, explain your algorithms and restore unfairly restricted accounts,” IYC said in a post on X. 

With no commitment made by either side, the meeting seems to have ended at a stale mate. The proceedings of the meeting were reported by Reuters. Inc42 has not been able to verify the information independently. We’ll update the story on the basis of comments from the tech giant. 

Meta’s Content Restrictions Surge In India

IYC has been protesting the recent increase in Meta’s content deletion over the past few months. Meta restricted access to more than 5.44 Mn items across Facebook and Instagram between January and June 2026, compared with around 41,400 in the preceding six months, marking an approximately 131X increase, according to its latest transparency disclosures.

The restrictions covered several categories, including online gaming, AI-generated content depicting prominent figures, threats to India’s sovereignty and integrity, gender-based harassment and the promotion of enmity between groups.

Meta has attributed the increase to changes in India’s IT rules, which require platforms to act on government takedown directions within shorter timelines.

India’s social media content moderation framework is primarily governed by the Information Technology Act, 2000, and the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021.

Under Rule 3(1)(d), intermediaries must remove or disable access to unlawful information after receiving a valid court order or a reasoned intimation from an authorised government officer. The provisions cover content relating to national security, public order and India’s sovereignty, among other grounds.

The government has tightened these requirements through successive amendments. In October 2025, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) notified amendments, effective November 15, requiring takedown notices to specify the legal provision invoked, the nature of the alleged unlawful act and the exact URL or electronic identifier of the content. The changes also introduced periodic reviews of government directions by senior officials.

In February 2026, the government further reduced the compliance window for intermediaries. An amendment effective February 20 cut the deadline to remove or disable access to specified unlawful content from 36 hours to three hours after receiving a valid court order or reasoned government intimation.

The shorter deadline has increased pressure on social media platforms to strengthen their content detection and enforcement systems, while raising questions about transparency and the potential for legitimate content to be restricted.

item.title: What Jensen Huang’s NVIDIA Return Means For India’s AI Players
item.dc:creator: Md Zakariya Khan
item.description: Jensen Huang’s return as NVIDIA CEO has eased concerns over leadership continuity at a key supplier to India’s AI ecosystem.…
item.content:encoded:
Jensen Huang’s return as NVIDIA CEO has eased concerns over leadership continuity at a key supplier to India’s AI ecosystem. However, analysts say it does little to address the Indian AI ecosystem’s dependence on the chipmaker or the constraints keeping advanced computing infrastructure expensive.

NVIDIA announced Huang’s reinstatement on November 23, following his resignation on November 12. US President Donald Trump welcomed the decision, describing Huang as a “national treasure”.

His departure had raised questions about NVIDIA’s investment plans, supply-chain management, pace of product innovation, and ability to retain talent. For Indian companies building AI infrastructure around its chips and software, continuity at NVIDIA offers greater certainty over the supplier’s direction.

“That said, NVIDIA is not a one-person company, but Jensen’s return does bring more certainty, and AI trade is perceiving this to be a good sign. There will be increased controls and governance at the company, which could impact Jensen’s internal influence in the company. This is something to watch for,” Gaurav Gupta, VP analyst at Gartner, told Inc42.

The company’s board has said its independent investigation will continue. NVIDIA has also formed a National Security and Export Control Committee and is seeking a chief compliance officer, adding oversight alongside Huang’s return.

For Indian buyers, however, leadership certainty does not necessarily translate into easier access to GPUs or lower procurement costs.

“The constraints are largely structural, driven by global demand, manufacturing capacity, advanced packaging, high-bandwidth memory availability and US export policies. These cannot be resolved through a leadership decision alone,” said Achyuta Ghosh, India market lead for HFS Research.

Dependence Beyond The Chips

NVIDIA’s presence in India spans AI computing infrastructure, software, data centres, startups, developer tools, and strategic partnerships.

Greyhound Research’s analysis of the IndiaAI Compute Portal put NVIDIA’s share at 81.6% of 44,077 listed compute units, ahead of Google, AMD, AWS, and Intel. This measures the composition of the cited portal dataset, rather than NVIDIA’s share of India’s total AI computing capacity.

A separate estimate by Counterpoint Research puts NVIDIA’s share of India’s high-end AI training and inference capacity at 85-90%.

The dependence extends beyond hardware to NVIDIA’s software ecosystem, particularly CUDA, which developers use to build and run GPU-accelerated applications. Indian startups, data centre operators, and large IT services companies are building AI infrastructure and solutions around this combination.

While competing chips are available, adopting them requires technical expertise to adapt software and optimise workloads. This makes diversification more involved than switching hardware suppliers.

“Indian operators would be vulnerable if certain decisions are made that cause NVIDIA to prioritise other projects as India might not be the priority,” Gupta added.

Smaller Indian data centre providers face a particular challenge because they compete with global hyperscalers with larger purchasing commitments and stronger supply-chain relationships.

To reduce this exposure, analysts recommend securing long-term procurement arrangements, exploring alternative accelerators where commercially viable, and developing the flexibility to run workloads across different hardware and cloud platforms.

“India’s goal should be to reduce excessive dependence on any single technology architecture while strengthening domestic capabilities in AI infrastructure management, software and optimisation,” Ghosh said.

Making Compute Investments Count

Beyond supplier diversification, Indian operators face another test – turning expensive infrastructure into commercially useful AI capacity.

Analysts expect GPU availability to improve gradually over the next 12-18 months, particularly for older-generation hardware and enterprise inference workloads. However, they do not expect a significant reduction in procurement costs for the latest high-performance GPUs, given continued strong global demand.

This could leave Indian operators paying a premium for the latest systems even as earlier-generation hardware becomes easier to procure. 

The response, analysts say, must extend beyond adding GPUs to improving utilisation, optimising workloads, reducing power consumption, and managing the cost of inference — the process of running trained AI models.

“The greater challenge is ensuring that infrastructure investments translate into enterprise AI adoption, domestic innovation and globally competitive AI capabilities. India’s AI infrastructure success should ultimately be measured by the AI capability and economic value it creates, not simply by the number of GPUs deployed,” Ghosh added.

More efficient models and better infrastructure utilisation could allow enterprises to run more AI workloads on the same computing capacity. Consequently, the cost of delivering AI services could decline even if GPU purchase prices remain elevated.

For Indian AI ecosystem players, Huang’s return provides greater leadership certainty at their dominant supplier. However, their longer-term economics will depend on how effectively they convert infrastructure investments into AI services that enterprises use and pay for.

item.title: [Update] Anthropic Rolls Out Claude Duet In India After US Launch
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Update | November 25, 2026, 18:50 IST Anthropic has expanded the research preview of Claude Duet, its AI-powered work assistant,…
item.content:encoded:
Update | November 25, 2026, 18:50 IST

Anthropic has expanded the research preview of Claude Duet, its AI-powered work assistant, to India, a month after its US launch.

Built on Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 model, Claude Duet can monitor users’ connected apps, identify tasks needing attention, and work in the background even when users are away from their devices. Its capabilities include scheduling meetings, tracking invoices, preparing financial forecasts, building dashboards, and developing web applications. 

In India, Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers can join a waitlist for the research preview. Team users can access the product through a public beta, while enterprise customers will get access through a private beta.

Claude Duet is available as a standalone app on iOS and Android, and through Claude’s website. It supports 35 languages, including Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Tamil, and Telugu. 

Original | October 22, 2026, 11:36 IST

Anthropic has unveiled Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent designed to monitor connected apps, prioritise tasks, and carry out work in the background, including when users switch off their devices.

The offering targets professionals and small business owners. Powered by Claude Opus 5.5, it is available as a research preview through a waitlist for Claude Pro and Max subscribers in the US.

Users can access Claude Duet through standalone iOS and Android apps or on Claude’s website. It is included in existing Pro and Max subscriptions but shares usage limits with other Claude products. Background checks count towards these limits, while complex assignments consume more usage, Anthropic said.

Unlike conventional AI chatbots, Claude Duet is designed to identify work that needs attention without waiting for a prompt. It sends users a daily briefing covering important items across connected apps, including emails and calendars, and provides updates when tasks are completed or require a decision.

Users can assign tasks through text or voice messages, ranging from scheduling meetings and drafting email replies to building dashboards, financial forecasts and web applications. The agent can also search past conversations and use existing Claude memories, skills and connected apps.

Claude Duet connects with more than 6,000 tools and plugins available through the Claude Marketplace, including Gmail, Slack, QuickBooks, Stripe, Gusto, LinkedIn, DocuSign, HubSpot and Shopify.

For instance, it can identify unpaid invoices through QuickBooks or Stripe and draft payment reminders. It can also prepare payroll information, draft job postings, create follow-up emails using customer and deal histories, and help businesses set up and manage online stores.

The agent runs on its own cloud-based virtual machine with a browser, allowing it to continue working even when users close the app or switch off their devices. Anthropic said it checks connected accounts every few hours rather than continuously, partly to limit subscription usage.

Claude Duet can also help users make business purchases through Link, Stripe’s digital wallet, and Shop Pay. Payments require user approval, while Link uses a virtual card to avoid sharing the user’s actual card number. Integration with 1Password for accessing saved website logins is also planned.

Anthropic said the agent requires approval before sending messages, making payments, signing documents or deleting information. Trading securities and transferring money between accounts remain prohibited, even with user approval. Users can disconnect apps, and only they can mark tasks as finished.

Safeguards And Early Limitations

Anthropic said Claude Duet includes safeguards designed to prevent unauthorised actions, prompt injection, and sensitive data leaks. Prompt injection involves malicious instructions hidden in content an agent encounters, such as emails or websites.

The protections include an automated system that assesses proposed actions and controls designed to keep passwords and sign-in tokens out of the agent’s direct view.

A separate message-checking system is designed to block requests to share highly sensitive information, including credit card numbers and government identification. Other sensitive information, such as health and personal finance details, can be shared only on explicit user instructions, Anthropic said.

The company said Claude Duet has undergone adversarial testing and external penetration testing, and is covered by its public bug bounty programme.

However, Anthropic acknowledged that the early version may misinterpret conversations, misjudge urgency, or miss information arriving between checks. It is currently better suited to work assignments than personal errands, such as booking tickets, and users cannot yet view its browser.

The launch adds to the growing competition in always-on AI agents that work across apps with limited human intervention. OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse target similar use cases, while Bengaluru-based Emergent’s Wingman handles tasks across email, calendars, and workplace software through WhatsApp and Telegram.

As agents gain access to more business systems, their permissions and accountability are also coming under scrutiny. Recently, CERT-In warned about unauthorised AI agent access to Indian organisations’ systems, highlighting the risks associated with deploying increasingly autonomous tools.

Anthropic said feedback from early users will inform further development. The research preview does not currently include Team and Enterprise subscribers.

item.title: Jio Platforms Launches JioAstro To Take On Astrotalk In India’s Booming Astrology Market

item.content:encoded:
Telecom major Jio Platforms has forayed into online astrology market with the launch of a dedicated offering, JioAstro. 

JioAstro generates birth charts using “Swiss Ephemeris calculations” and further gives personalised insights by advanced AI trained in Vedic astrology. JioAstro is available in English, Hindi, Marathi and Gujarati. 

The company hasn’t disclosed which large language models (LLMs) power the platform, whether it relies on proprietary models or third-party AI infrastructure.

While JioAstro is accessible through its website and has a listing on Google Play, its terms describe the mobile app as an invite-only prototype available through the internal testing track.

With the AI-powered vedic astrology platform, Jio takes on the likes of consumer startups Astrotalk, AstroSage, among others, who have already been in this space for some years. 

One of the most renowned astrology platforms and India’s 133rd unicorn, Astrotalk, was delisted from Apple’s App Store on November 4. Sources told Inc42 that the spiritual tech startup is in discussions with Apple over the delisting. The app, however, remains unavailable on the platform.

The broader spiritual tech ecosystem has seen growing investor interest, with startups raising capital to expand their offerings.

Earlier this year, Astrotalk joined India’s unicorn club following an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) buyback at a $1 Bn valuation. Back then, the startup also said its annual revenue run rate (ARR) had crossed ₹2,500 Cr.

Other startups like AppsForBharat, VAMA, MyNaksh, Sanctuary, AstroSure, among others, have also raised investor support in recent times. 

More recently, Kolkata-based Utsav raised ₹36 Cr ($3.8 Mn) in a Series A round led by Atomic Capital, with existing investors India Quotient and Equanimity Investments also participating.

The stars of the Indian digital astrology market are on the rise. The segment is estimated to be worth $390 Mn in 2026 and is projected to reach $2.32 Bn by 2032, registering a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 34.61%, as per MarkNtel Advisors.

item.title: SoftBank Investment Director Narendra Rathi Steps Down
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: SoftBank Investment Advisers’ Narendra Rathi is stepping down from his role as investment director in the company by the end…
item.content:encoded:
SoftBank Investment Advisers’ Narendra Rathi is stepping down from his role as investment director in the company by the end of this year, sources told Inc42.

ET reported the development first. 

As per the report, Rathi intends to launch a public markets fund that will bet on India becoming a significant participant in the AI infrastructure build-out. Rathi’s new fund will focus on industrial companies, including smaller, lesser-known listed firms that could benefit from the growing number of data centres in India, the report said.

Inc42 has reached out to Rathi for comments on the exit. The story will be updated based on his response.

As per his LinkedIn profile, Rathi joined SoftBank in April 2019 as an investment associate and has served the company under various roles for close to eight years. In 2022, while SoftBank’s India head Sumer Juneja was elevated to oversee investments in Europe, Middle-East and Africa (EMEA) markets, Rathi along with Sarthak Misra were assigned the duty of assisting Juneja.

Prior to this, he worked with Morgan Stanley for more than five years as an analyst and associate. He has also been previously associated with companies like Nomura Services India and i3 consulting.

SoftBank is one of the major foreign investors in the country and has so far deployed nearly $16 Bn in Indian startups. Having funded nearly a fifth of India’s 100+ unicorns, SoftBank has previously backed the likes of Flipkart, OYO, Delhivery, OfBusiness, FirstCry and Meesho.

In the past few months, SoftBank has diluted its stake in listed companies like Delhivery, Lenskart, Meesho and Ola Electric.

SoftBank swung to the red and posted a net loss of nearly $7 Bn in Q2 FY26 against a profit of $15.9 Bn in the year ago period. The investment firm also reported $14.1 Bn in net sales in the quarter under review, up 15.6% from $12.2 Bn in Q2 FY25.

Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that there has been a rise in exits at VC firms in this month, where Nexus VP’s partner Anup Gupta is stepping away from his role, while Fireside Ventures’ cofounder Vinay Singh and principal Prayag Mohanty also resigned from their positions.

item.title: Lok Capital Announces First Close Of Fund V At $130 Mn
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Social impact focused investor Lok Capital has raised over $130 Mn in the first close of its latest AIF, Fund…
item.content:encoded:
Social impact focused investor Lok Capital has raised over $130 Mn in the first close of its latest AIF, Fund V. The target corpus of the fund was earlier set to be in the range of $200-250 Mn. 

The fund will focus on investing in companies focused on financial inclusion, i.e. expanding access to financial services for underserved segments, and climate and sustainability across agriculture, mobility, logistics, manufacturing, and consumer markets.

Via the fund, Lok Capital plans to back 10-12 companies with established business models and sustainable revenue traction with cheques averaging around $8-25 Mn and co-investing in rounds of up to $50 Mn, MD Rajat Bansal told Mint.  

The International Finance Corporation, European Investment Bank, and the Dutch government’s Entrepreneurial Development Bank (FMO) have all disclosed proposed investments in Lok Capital’s latest fund. 

The IFC has proposed an equity investment of up to $20 Mn and an additional co-investment envelope of up to $20 Mn, while the EIB has proposed to invest around $50 Mn. FMO has disclosed a potential investment commitment of around $15 Mn. 

Founded in 2004 by Vishal Mehta, Venky Natarajan, and Donald Peck, Lok Capital has launched four funds to date with a cumulative corpus of $347 Mn. It has made over 47 investments till date and claims that 8 of its invested companies have gone public.

The investment firm’s portfolio includes companies like Moneyview, RenewBuy, Akshayakalpa, Mintifi, Marut Drones, and Anveshan. Beyond new-age tech companies, the investor has also backed Jana Small Finance Bank, Utkarsh Small Finance Bank, Suryodya, among others. 

Most recently, it co-led egg brand Henfruit’s $15 Mn Series A round alongside DSG Consumer Partners and RPSG Capital Ventures. 

The investor also claims to have delivered a complete exit on the first two funds and expects to liquidate the remaining investments from Fund III over the next year, while it has started delivering the exit proceeds from Fund IV to its LPs.

item.title: PhonePe Revives IPO Plans, Eyes March 2027 Listing At Up To $15 Bn Valuation
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: Walmart-backed fintech major PhonePe has revived its IPO plans and restarted discussions with investment bankers, targeting a March 2027 listing…
item.content:encoded:
Walmart-backed fintech major PhonePe has revived its IPO plans and restarted discussions with investment bankers, targeting a March 2027 listing at a valuation of $12 Bn to $15 Bn, sources told Inc42.

The Bengaluru-based company plans to file updated IPO papers by December-end for an offer for sale of up to ₹12,000 Cr ($1.3 Bn).

Notably, PhonePe was valued at $14.5 Bn during General Atlantic’s $600 Mn secondary investment in 2025.

Sources said PhonePe expects greater clarity by December-end on two regulatory issues affecting the company’s business – the merchant discount rate (MDR) framework for UPI transactions and the 30% market-share cap for third-party UPI apps.

A possible extension or relaxation of the cap could ease a regulatory overhang ahead of the proposed listing, the sources said.

PhonePe declined to comment on the IPO development. The Economic Times first reported on the revival of its listing plans.

The renewed push comes after PhonePe paused its IPO plans in March, citing geopolitical uncertainty and volatility in global capital markets. At the time, the company said it would restart the process once markets stabilised. 

The rally in Indian equities and foreign portfolio investors’ return to net buying appear to have given PhonePe greater confidence to revive its listing plans. 

Growth And Profitability In Focus

PhonePe is seeing stronger growth in lending and operating revenue, the sources said. The company’s lending business has grown around 100%, while operating revenue has increased 35%-40% QoQ. The company is also expected to report a net profit, they added.

This would mark a turnaround from FY26, when PhonePe reported a net loss of ₹2,792 Cr. Operating revenue rose 11.5% to ₹7,920.5 Cr from ₹7,105 Cr in FY25. 

The lending business offers PhonePe a route to diversify revenue beyond its core payments operations. Its growth and contribution to profitability will be relevant to the company’s pitch to public market investors. 

UPI Rules Remain Key

Beyond financial performance, the regulatory outlook remains central to PhonePe’s IPO preparations.

Introducing MDR on select UPI transactions could create an additional revenue stream for payment companies. However, whether such charges will be introduced remains uncertain.

The other issue is the National Payments Corporation of India’s (NPCI) 30% cap on UPI transaction volumes handled by individual third-party application providers (TPAPs). NPCI had extended the compliance deadline for existing apps exceeding the cap to December 31, 2026.

PhonePe operates above the threshold, making any further extension or relaxation significant for its growth plans ahead of the proposed public market debut. 

Its renewed listing push also coincides with IPO preparations at payments infrastructure major Razorpay.

Razorpay has received SEBI’s approval for its proposed ₹5,000 Cr–₹6,000 Cr public offering. It is targeting a valuation of around $5 Bn (₹47,000 Cr), with a listing likely between January and March 2027, sources previously told Inc42. The timeline could put its debut ahead of PhonePe’s proposed March listing.

item.title: PayU India Turns Adjusted EBITDA Profitable In H1 FY27
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Prosus-owned fintech company PayU India swung to an adjusted EBITDA profit of $12 Mn in the first half of FY27…
item.content:encoded:
Prosus-owned fintech company PayU India swung to an adjusted EBITDA profit of $12 Mn in the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), compared to a loss of $1 Mn in the year-ago period, driven by growth in its lending business. 

However, adjusted EBIT remained negative at $3 Mn, although this was an improvement from a loss of $15 Mn in H1 FY26. 

The bottom line improvements come despite a 3.3% decline in its revenue to $384 Mn from $397 Mn in the last year period.

However, disclosing the numbers, Prosus said PayU’s revenue grew 6% in local currency, excluding the impact of mergers and acquisitions (M&A). Excluding strategically cancelled merchant accounts, revenue growth stood at 13% and transaction volumes grew 20% in local currency.

The development comes as Prosus reported a mixed performance across its India portfolio, with the Dutch technology investor also disclosing an 8.6% fully diluted stake in Sachin Bansal-led fintech startup Navi following a $100 Mn investment. 

Separately, it recognised a $103 Mn impairment on an unnamed listed equity-accounted investment in its Indian ecosystem.

The distinction is important as PayU has been exiting merchant accounts that do not meet its profitability requirements, affecting reported payments revenue but improving the quality of its business.

PayU’s Credit Business Drives Profitability

PayU’s payments business continued to account for the larger share of its revenue, contributing $265 Mn in H1 FY27. 

However, payments revenue declined 12% YoY in dollar terms, or 4% in local currency, reflecting the timing of the Diwali festive season and strategic merchant exits. Despite the revenue decline, the payments segment’s gross margin improved to 25% from 23% in H1 FY26. 

In contrast, PayU’s credit business’ revenue grew by 24% YoY to $119 Mn. This business also turned adjusted EBITDA positive, recording a profit of $10 Mn against a loss of $3 Mn in the year-ago period. Credit revenue grew 36% in local currency.

The lending business accounted for around 31% of PayU’s total revenue during the period, compared to 24% a year earlier. Its credit assets under management (AUM) also grew 20% YoY.

Prosus Completes $100 Mn Navi Investment

At a group level, Prosus disclosed that it completed its $100 Mn investment in Navi in November 2026, acquiring a 9.1% ownership stake in the fintech company.

The investment follows approval from the Competition Commission of India (CCI). Prosus said it would account for Navi as an equity-accounted investment, citing the significant influence it holds through board representation.

Based on the $100 Mn investment and the fully diluted ownership percentage, the transaction implies an equity valuation of approximately $1.2 Bn for Navi, as per Inc42’s calculations.

Separately, Prosus recognised a $103 Mn impairment on a listed equity-accounted investment in its India ecosystem during H1 FY27, following a significant decline in the investment’s market value relative to its carrying value.

The investor attributed the broader market pressure to factors including higher oil prices, elevated global interest rates and a weaker rupee.

Prosus reported total impairments of $136 Mn on equity-accounted investments during the period. Of this, $103 Mn related to the listed investment in its India ecosystem, while the remaining $33 Mn was associated with unlisted investments in its other ecosystem.

To note, this impairment reflects a reduction in the carrying value of Prosus’ investment and does not represent a loss incurred by the portfolio company itself.

The disclosures come as Prosus continues to reshape its portfolio through investments, operational improvements and capital allocation. The company reported 59% growth in ecosystem revenue to $5.7 Bn in H1 FY27, while ecosystem adjusted EBITDA stood at $492 Mn, compared to $530 Mn in the year-ago period.

In India, Prosus said that its ecosystem now reaches more than 500 Mn annual users and processes around 450 Mn orders a month, with PayU’s payment infrastructure embedded across several portfolio businesses.

item.title: Film Body Seeks Ban On Pakistani Show’s Netflix Release In India
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) has written to prime minister Narendra Modi seeking a ban on releasing the…
item.content:encoded:
The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) has written to prime minister Narendra Modi seeking a ban on releasing the Pakistani series “Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo” on Netflix India on December 4, 2026. 

The body has also demanded a “strong, permanent law” to keep Pakistani content off Indian television, OTT platforms and cinema.

The letter, dated November 24 and signed by AICWA president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta, was shared by news agency ANI on X. It is copied to information and broadcasting minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and to Netflix India.

AICWA’s four demands are listed below: 

  • that the series is not released or streamed in India on December 4 or any other date
  • that all OTT and streaming platforms strictly comply with the May 8, 2025 advisory
  • that the permanent law be enacted
  • that platforms be made to understand that commercial interest can never come before national security and the sentiments of the martyrs’ families

The letter also appeals to Netflix India and other OTT platforms to state clearly in their social media posts that such content will not be shown in India. 

It ends with the line: “No Pakistani face, voice or story has a place on Indian screens.”

Netflix is yet to issue a statement on this. Inc42 has reached out to the company and the story will be updated based on their response.

AICWA claimed that the series stars Pakistani actors — Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan and Hania Aamir — have spoken against India at times of high tension between the two countries. The association said its letter speaks for the “140 Cr people” of the country.

The letter’s central argument is that Netflix’s release would run directly against the government’s stance. AICWA pointed to the information and broadcasting ministry’s May 2025 advisory, which asked OTT platforms and streaming services to stop streaming Pakistan-origin web series, films, songs and podcasts. 

Back then, the ministry said that several terrorist attacks in India have been established to have cross-border linkages with Pakistan-based state and non-state actors. ICWA highlighted that the government itself had banned Pakistani artists from working in the Indian film industry after the recent Pulwama attack. 

Notably, this pattern of cancelling things associated with Pakistan is not only limited to content. Last year, trade body CAIT asked the government to ban Pakistani flags and merchandise on ecommerce platforms. The Central Consumer Protection Authority then issued notices to Amazon, Flipkart, Etsy and three other platforms over the sale of such products.

item.title: OpenAI, SpaceX Backer VU Venture Partners Enters Indian Startup Market
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: US-based VC firm VU Venture Partners, which has backed tech giants like OpenAI, SpaceX, Uber at early stages, has entered…
item.content:encoded:
US-based VC firm VU Venture Partners, which has backed tech giants like OpenAI, SpaceX, Uber at early stages, has entered the Indian market. The firm will look to back early-stage startups (seed, Series A levels) and its ticket sizes would range from $100K to $1 Mn.

It will look to build an India portfolio concentrated around nine sectors — AI, robotics, space and defence, advanced computing, healthcare, consumer, enterprise, fintech and industrials, including proptech and climate.

The firm said that it will deploy capital through its global fund and investor syndicate, which comprises more than 8,000 accredited investors. 

Alongside making equity investments in the world’s third largest startup ecosystem, VU Venture Partners has also introduced its investor accelerator programme, Venture University, in India. 

For context, Venture University offers an 11-week investor education programme comprising a 40-hour VC workshop and modules, followed by an apprenticeship lasting approximately three to 12 months with VU Venture Partners. 

The accelerator will accept up to 25 participants per quarter, including aspiring venture capital professionals, angel investors, family offices, emerging and established fund managers, and fund-of-funds. The programme’s first cohort is scheduled to begin on April 5, 2027, with applications now open. 

The firm said its previous accelerator cohorts have collectively invested more than $80 Mn across 125+ companies, including over 12 unicorns. Its portfolio includes companies such as Neuralink, Anduril, Figure and Varda, among others.

Overall, VU Venture Partners’ senior investment team has deployed more than $2 Bn across 300+ companies, backed over 30 unicorns and recorded more than 20 multi-billion-dollar exits, according to the company.

The firm’s India expansion will be supported by Anaina Malik, a partner on its India team, alongside members of its Hong Kong and Australia teams.

VU Venture Partners said it has already made investments in India, including diagnostics startup Redcliffe Labs and hospitality startup goSTOPS.

The expansion comes as global venture capital firms continue to explore India’s startup ecosystem, particularly in AI, deeptech, fintech and other emerging sectors. 

VU Venture Partners’ India expansion comes amid renewed interest from global investors in the country’s startup ecosystem, with several firms committing fresh capital or setting up investment vehicles focused on emerging technology sectors. 

In February 2026, General Catalyst announced plans to invest $5 Bn in Indian startups over five years, targeting sectors such as AI, defence, healthcare, fintech and industrials. 

Qualcomm Ventures also committed up to $150 Mn through a dedicated strategic AI venture fund for Indian startups, with a focus on AI applications across automotive, robotics, IoT and mobile technologies.

Accel also closed its ninth India-focused fund with a $550 Mn corpus in August, targeting AI, deeptech and other early-stage businesses. The fund was part of a larger $3.5 Bn global fundraising exercise and came roughly 18 months after its previous India fund.

item.title: Foxconn India Unit Faces Insolvency Plea Over ₹143 Cr In Alleged Dues
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Apple iPhone assembler Foxconn Technology Group’s India unit is facing an insolvency petition from BCD Emprasa LLP, which is seeking…
item.content:encoded:
Apple iPhone assembler Foxconn Technology Group’s India unit is facing an insolvency petition from BCD Emprasa LLP, which is seeking nearly ₹143 Cr (around $15 Mn) in alleged unpaid dues, interest, service charges, and damages.

BCD filed the petition before the Chennai bench of the NCLT in August against Foxconn Hon Hai Technology India Mega Development Pvt Ltd, Bloomberg reported, citing the filing.

The claim, calculated as of July 8, relates to alleged defaults on rent and utility payments for accommodation leased to house employees working at Foxconn’s Bengaluru facility.

The petition comes amid reported payment delays affecting about half a dozen local vendors working with Foxconn’s India unit.

Queries sent by Inc42 to BCD Emprasa remained unanswered till the time of publication. The story will be updated on receiving their responses.

Replying to Inc42’s queries, the company claimed that the dispute arose from “the supplier’s failure to meet agreed contractual requirements and quality standards. Despite repeated requests for corrective action, the outstanding issues remain unresolved.”

“As the matter is now subject to legal proceedings, Foxconn will take appropriate steps to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests through the legal process and will refrain from commenting further on the specifics of the case,” it added.

Employee Housing Dispute

Under an agreement signed in April 2024, BCD leased 700 residential units to accommodate Foxconn’s female employees. The agreement required rent to be paid regardless of occupancy and included a lock-in period extending until July 2026, according to the filing cited by Bloomberg.

BCD alleged that Foxconn failed to clear an invoice due in May 2025 and did not agree to appoint an arbitrator to resolve the dispute.

In a response to Bloomberg, BCD said the alleged defaults caused significant financial and commercial losses, adding that the matter was sub judice before the NCLT.

Other Vendors Await Payments

Beyond BCD, at least four other vendors have reportedly been waiting for several months to more than a year for Foxconn to clear their dues, the report said, citing sources.

Several of these vendors were engaged in construction-related work at the company’s Bengaluru facility and had been working with the iPhone manufacturer for the first time.

The departure of certain non-Indian employees also reportedly slowed down the processing of payments to local contractors.

The disputes come amid Foxconn’s continued investment in its Indian manufacturing operations.

In June, its Singapore subsidiary invested $37.2 Mn in Foxconn Hon Hai Technology India Mega Development.

The company has also been expanding its component manufacturing ambitions. In May last year, it infused nearly $1.5 Bn into its Tamil Nadu-registered entity Yuzhan Technology (India). It subsequently explored setting up another unit in the state to manufacture iPhone enclosures.

item.title: Kalyan Krishnamurthy To Exit Flipkart, Balaji Thiagarajan To Lead In Interim
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Walmart-owned Flipkart Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy is set to step down after being asked to leave by Walmart leadership, sources…
item.content:encoded:
Walmart-owned Flipkart Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy is set to step down after being asked to leave by Walmart leadership, sources told Inc42.

Flipkart confirmed his departure in a statement, marking a leadership transition after nearly a decade under his watch. The company said it would announce his successor in the coming weeks.

Until then, chief product and technology officer Balaji Thiagarajan and Flipkart’s board will lead the organisation in the interim.

Flipkart called an emergency town hall amid speculation over his exit, sources told Inc42. Moneycontrol was first to report about Krishnamurthy’s departure.

In an internal memo, Flipkart said Krishnamurthy’s last day with the company will be on December 4.

A former Tiger Global executive, Krishnamurthy became Flipkart’s CEO in January 2017, before Walmart acquired a majority stake in the ecommerce giant in 2018. He has served as group CEO since 2018.

Founded by Sachin Bansal and Binny Bansal, Flipkart expanded under Krishnamurthy’s leadership while competing with Amazon and Meesho and building new businesses under Walmart’s ownership.

“Both Flipkart and Walmart are better because of Kalyan. We are grateful for his leadership, the governance he instilled and his many contributions to the company. We wish him nothing but the best as he moves on to his next adventure,” said Chris Nicholas, president and CEO of Walmart International.

Nicholas added that Walmart remained confident about Flipkart’s future and its potential to help customers in India save money and live better.

In his statement, Krishnamurthy said it had been a privilege to be part of Flipkart’s journey and highlighted the importance of ethics, integrity, and governance in building the business.

“Our team has helped change how millions of Indians shop, expanding choice and creating opportunities for sellers, entrepreneurs and businesses across the country. I’m grateful to the colleagues, sellers and partners who have been part of this journey. Flipkart has a strong foundation and an exciting future, and I wish the team every success,” he said.

IPO Delays, ESOP Concerns, And Senior Exits

The transition comes while Flipkart balances its listing ambitions and expansion plans with employee concerns over ESOP liquidity and Walmart’s push for better financial performance.

Earlier this year, Flipkart reportedly deferred its IPO until at least 2028. Walmart wants the ecommerce giant to achieve EBITDA breakeven by the end of FY27 before considering a public listing or another external fundraise. The reported directive followed Walmart CEO John Furner’s visit to Bengaluru. 

The IPO postponement followed Flipkart’s reverse flip from Singapore to India in March 2026, which removed a structural hurdle to a potential domestic listing.

The delay has also sharpened concerns over employee stock option (ESOP) liquidity. In October, former executives, including ex-Myntra CEO Mukesh Bansal, former Flipkart chief business officer Ankit Nagori, and former CFO Sanjay Baweja, wrote to Walmart’s board seeking fair treatment and a full cash-out opportunity for their vested options.

Sources earlier told Inc42 that some senior executives left because they could not see a clear opportunity to liquidate their ESOPs, while others moved to new organisations or explored entrepreneurial ventures.

As Inc42 reported in October, Flipkart had seen 14 senior-level departures over the preceding year, including three vice presidents whose exits were then pending — Kanchan Mishra, VP of smartphones; Amit Sachan, VP of product and technology; and Kamal Chopra, VP of corporate.

Expansion Across Consumer Services

Meanwhile, alongside its profitability push, Flipkart is seeking to widen its consumer business through quick commerce, food delivery, entertainment, and ticketing.

Quick commerce is central to this expansion. UBS earlier projected that Flipkart Minutes could add around 1,000 dark stores by mid-2027, potentially taking its network to around 2,000, while competing with Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, and Zepto.

The company has also been exploring short-form scripted shows and microdramas, adding entertainment to its diversification plans

In food delivery, sources earlier told Inc42 that Flipkart planned a Bengaluru launch by mid-August. The company subsequently began employee trials of its service, branded ‘Eat-in by Minutes’, and was targeting an October-end public launch.

Flipkart has also considered entering India’s movie and live-event ticketing market ahead of a potential IPO.

On the financial front, Flipkart Group reported an 18.2% jump in consolidated revenue from operations to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in FY26, compared with ₹1.23 Lakh Cr in the previous fiscal.

Meanwhile, its consolidated net loss narrowed 2.1% to ₹8,468 Cr in FY26, from ₹8,646 Cr in FY25.

item.title: Aeravti Ventures Launches ₹300 Cr Fund II, Marks First Close At Over ₹150 Cr
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Bengaluru-based VC firm Aeravti Ventures has launched its second fund, Aeravti Ventures II, with a target corpus of ₹300 Cr,…
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based VC firm Aeravti Ventures has launched its second fund, Aeravti Ventures II, with a target corpus of ₹300 Cr, securing commitments exceeding ₹150 Cr at its first close.

The Category II AIF has attracted capital from LPs of its maiden fund, corporates, family offices, high-net-worth individuals (HNIs), and ultra HNIs. 

The firm expects to complete the final close within six months and said the capital would be deployed over the next 10 years.

Fund II will back 9-10 early-stage startups across three broad themes: food security, health infrastructure, and physical infrastructure. Its focus will span agriculture and allied sectors, biosciences, life sciences, advanced manufacturing, waste management, and energy.

The launch expands Aeravti’s investment strategy into physical infrastructure-led businesses, alongside its existing focus on food and healthcare.

The new fund will invest from pre-seed to pre-Series A, with a preference for leading pre-seed and seed rounds.

Backing Startups Beyond Seed Stage

Aeravti plans to write initial cheques of ₹6 Cr to ₹10 Cr per startup, retaining capacity to invest another 2-3 times the initial amount in subsequent rounds. Follow-on investments would typically be considered 12-18 months after the initial investment, with cheque sizes of ₹10–25 Cr.

The fund has already backed three startups but the firm did not disclose their names.

Aeravti Ventures managing partner Rishabh Singh told Inc42 that founder resilience is the firm’s most important consideration when evaluating early-stage businesses.

The strategy builds on its maiden fund, which achieved a final close of ₹76 Cr and is fully deployed across seven startups. Aeravti led the seed rounds in all seven companies.

The firm had announced the first close of its maiden fund in May 2023, when it was targeting a ₹100 Cr corpus to back emerging technology startups across deeptech, biosciences, agritech, climate, and enterprise tech. 

Discussing the fundraising environment, Singh said raising capital has become difficult for venture funds in India and globally, reinforcing the need for investment firms to sharpen their focus.

He cautioned against pursuing emerging sectors simply because they are attracting attention elsewhere, arguing that India needs to develop its own VC and startup ecosystem rather than following the US playbook.
